questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: The University of Benin (UNIBEN) is located in which state?
questions.explanation: UNIBEN is located in Benin City, the capital of Edo State, and is one of Nigeria's first-generation federal universities.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: In what year was the institution now known as the University of Benin founded?
questions.explanation: The University of Benin traces its origin to 1970, when it was established as a full university, having started as an institute of technology in 1970 under federal government ownership.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Benin City, home to UNIBEN, was historically the capital of which powerful pre-colonial African kingdom?
questions.explanation: Benin City was the historic capital of the Benin Kingdom (also called the Benin Empire), one of the oldest and most highly organised states in West African history.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What title is given to the traditional ruler of the Benin Kingdom?
questions.explanation: The traditional ruler of the Benin Kingdom holds the title 'Oba of Benin', a position with a long unbroken royal lineage dating back many centuries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: The Benin Bronzes, celebrated worldwide for their craftsmanship, were traditionally produced using which metalworking technique?
questions.explanation: The Benin Bronzes were crafted using the lost-wax casting technique, a sophisticated method that produced highly detailed bronze and brass plaques and sculptures for the Benin royal court.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What were many of the Benin Bronzes originally created to depict or commemorate?
options: The history, rituals, and achievements of the Oba and the royal court
questions.explanation: The bronzes and plaques served largely as historical and ceremonial records, depicting the Oba, chiefs, warriors, and important events of the Benin royal court.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: In what year did British forces launch the punitive expedition that led to the looting of thousands of Benin Bronzes from the royal palace?
questions.explanation: The 1897 British Punitive Expedition sacked Benin City and looted thousands of artefacts, including the Benin Bronzes, many of which ended up in Western museums.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which present-day Nigerian ethnic group is most closely associated with the historic Benin Kingdom and Benin City?
questions.explanation: The Edo (also called Bini) people are the principal ethnic group historically associated with the Benin Kingdom and the traditional custodians of its culture.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes a key reason UNIBEN is often referred to by the motto phrase 'Knowledge for Service'?
options: It is the name of the university's founding vice-chancellor
It refers only to the university's teaching hospital
It was the original 1970 name of the institution
It reflects the university's stated mission of applying knowledge to serve society
questions.explanation: 'Knowledge for Service' is UNIBEN's official motto, reflecting its mission of producing graduates and research that serve national development.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Edo State, where UNIBEN is situated, shares a border with which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Edo State shares a border with Delta State to the south and east, among other neighbouring states such as Kogi and Ondo.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the capital city of Edo State?
questions.explanation: Benin City serves as both the capital of Edo State and the historic seat of the Benin Kingdom.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: The ancient Benin moats and walls, once among the largest man-made earthworks in the world, were built primarily for what purpose?
options: Defence and demarcation of the kingdom's boundaries
questions.explanation: The Benin Walls and moats, known as the Iya, were extensive earthworks built largely for defensive purposes and to mark territorial boundaries within the kingdom.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is a well-known annual festival celebrated by the Benin people, honouring the Oba and ancestral traditions?
questions.explanation: The Igue Festival is an important annual traditional festival of the Benin people, held to honour the Oba and renew the kingdom's spiritual and cultural bonds.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which arm of government in Nigeria is primarily responsible for interpreting laws and administering justice?
questions.explanation: The Judiciary is the arm of government responsible for interpreting laws and adjudicating disputes, distinct from the law-making Legislature and law-enforcing Executive.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for the Nigerian legislative chamber that represents individual constituencies at the federal level, alongside the Senate?
questions.explanation: The House of Representatives, together with the Senate, forms Nigeria's bicameral National Assembly, with members representing federal constituencies.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following countries shares a land border with Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Nigeria shares land borders with Cameroon, Niger, Chad, and Benin Republic; Ghana, South Africa, and Kenya are not bordering countries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the largest desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara Desert, spanning much of North Africa, is the largest hot desert in the world.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary function of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)?
options: Organising and supervising elections in Nigeria
questions.explanation: INEC is Nigeria's independent body responsible for organising, conducting, and supervising elections at the federal and state levels.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is a major cash crop historically associated with Edo State and the wider Niger Delta fringe region?
questions.explanation: Edo State, particularly around Benin City, has long been associated with rubber cultivation and processing, alongside oil palm production.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the chemical symbol for oxygen?
questions.explanation: Oxygen's chemical symbol is 'O', representing the element on the periodic table (the common gas is the diatomic molecule O2).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet'?
questions.explanation: Mars is called the 'Red Planet' because of the iron oxide (rust) that gives its surface a reddish appearance.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is Nigeria's national football team commonly nicknamed?
questions.explanation: Nigeria's senior men's national football team is popularly known as the Super Eagles, distinct from Ghana's Black Stars and Cameroon's Indomitable Lions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which international body is primarily responsible for global public health coordination?
questions.explanation: The WHO is the United Nations agency specifically responsible for coordinating international public health matters.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for a system of government headed by a king or queen whose powers are limited by a constitution?
questions.explanation: A constitutional monarchy is a system in which a monarch serves as head of state, but their powers are limited and defined by a constitution, unlike an absolute monarchy.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a non-communicable disease?
questions.explanation: Diabetes is a non-communicable (non-infectious) disease, unlike tuberculosis, malaria, and cholera, which are caused by infectious agents.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the largest country in the world by land area?
questions.explanation: Russia is the largest country in the world by land area, spanning parts of both Europe and Asia.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary role of a Vice-Chancellor in a Nigerian university, such as UNIBEN?
options: Serving as the elected student union president
Serving as the chief executive and academic head of the university
Managing only the university's sports facilities
Serving as an external auditor of the university's accounts
questions.explanation: A Vice-Chancellor is the chief executive and principal academic officer of a Nigerian university, responsible for its overall administration and academic direction.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which regulatory body is responsible for accrediting academic programmes in Nigerian universities?
options: The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB)
The Federal Ministry of Education alone, with no separate agency
questions.explanation: The NUC is the regulatory body responsible for approving and accrediting academic programmes offered by Nigerian universities, ensuring they meet minimum quality standards.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for the total value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given period?
questions.explanation: GDP specifically measures the value of goods and services produced within a country's borders, regardless of the nationality of the producers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Nigerian playwright and author was the first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature?
questions.explanation: Wole Soyinka won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986, becoming the first African laureate in that category.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What does the abbreviation 'NAFDAC' stand for in the Nigerian context?
options: Nigerian Agency for Food and Drug Coordination
National Authority for Food, Drugs, and Cosmetics
National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
National Association for Drug and Chemical Control
questions.explanation: NAFDAC regulates and controls the manufacture, importation, and sale of food, drugs, and related products in Nigeria.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for a persistent, sustained rise in the general price level of goods and services in an economy?
questions.explanation: Inflation describes an ongoing, generalised increase in prices across an economy, the opposite of deflation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary aim of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)?
options: Creating a single market for goods and services across African countries to boost intra-African trade
Restricting all trade between African nations
questions.explanation: AfCFTA aims to create a single continental market for goods and services, boosting intra-African trade by reducing tariffs and other trade barriers among member states.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is a key function of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) relating to currency?
options: Issuing and regulating the country's currency (the Naira)
Setting the retail price of consumer goods
questions.explanation: One of the CBN's core functions is the sole authority to issue and regulate Nigeria's legal tender currency, the Naira.
